purpose: Classify the binary three-orbit relations induced by orbit-rigid C4 interaction bundles and test whether the rigid layer collapses to a generically tractable affine/majority/semilattice language. It does not: the finite rigid-bundle catalog yields 120 distinct binary relations, and their primitive-positive binary closure under conjunction, argument reversal and one-variable relational composition is all 2^9=512 binary relations on {0,1,2}. In particular NEQ_3 has a constant-size pp definition using three explicit orbit-rigid bundles.

domain_and_bundle_language.valid_bundle: B is a subset of the 16 port pairs (p,q) in {0,1,2,3}^2 with every left and right port used at most twice, matching the Hamiltonian degree-two bound at an original vertex.
domain_and_bundle_language.relative_gain_set: S_B(a,b)={h in S3 : h(T_a[p]) != T_b[q] for every (p,q) in B}.
domain_and_bundle_language.orbit_rigid: B is orbit-rigid iff every nonempty S_B(a,b) is a singleton.

exhaustive_catalog.note: Counts are for literal labelled port bundles/relations, not quotienting by dihedral port symmetries or orbit-label permutations.

pp_operations.intersection: R AND S on the same ordered pair corresponds to conjunction R(x,y) and S(x,y).
pp_operations.converse: R^T corresponds to swapping the two variables/arguments.
pp_operations.composition: R composed S = {(x,y): exists z, R(x,z) AND S(z,y)}; this is one existentially quantified auxiliary three-state variable.
pp_operations.closure_result: Starting from the 120 rigid orbit relations (and equality, which variable identification supplies for free), exhaustive closure under these operations reaches all 512 binary relations on a three-element domain.

explicit_NEQ_certificate.identity: NEQ_3(x,y) iff A(x,y) AND exists z [ B(x,z) AND C(z,y) ].
explicit_NEQ_certificate.verification: B composed C equals NEQ_3 union {(0,0)}; intersecting with A deletes exactly (0,0), leaving the six off-diagonal pairs. All A,B,C bundles are orbit-rigid by direct S3 enumeration.

main_theorem.name: RIGID_C4_ORBIT_LANGUAGE_PP_DEFINES_ALL_BINARY_THREE_STATE_RELATIONS
main_theorem.statement: Let Gamma_rigid be the set of binary orbit-admissibility relations A_B induced by valid orbit-rigid labelled C4 port bundles. Every binary relation R subseteq {0,1,2}^2 has a primitive-positive definition from Gamma_rigid using conjunction, variable identification/reversal and existentially quantified intermediate variables.
finite_proof: Enumerate every valid labelled port bundle B and every orbit pair (a,b). Evaluate all six relative gains h in S3 exactly; retain B when each nonempty S_B(a,b) is a singleton and record A_B.
The resulting finite base consists of 120 distinct binary relations.
Repeatedly add intersections, converses and relational compositions. The checker reaches exactly 512 distinct masks, which is the entire binary relation universe on a three-element domain.
The explicit three-bundle certificate independently pp-defines NEQ_3 without relying on the full closure count.

complexity_consequence.generic_CSP: The unrestricted abstract CSP over Gamma_rigid is NP-hard: ordinary graph 3-colourability has one NEQ_3 constraint per graph edge, and the displayed constant-size pp gadget replaces each NEQ_3 by three Gamma_rigid atoms plus one existential three-state variable with only constant blowup.
complexity_consequence.important_source_firewall: This generic CSP reduction does NOT yet prove NP-hardness of the source-restricted smooth-C4 Hamiltonian quotient itself. A pp formula may wire rigid bundle atoms in a constraint graph/port pattern that is not realizable as one Hamiltonian Euler-tour quotient with the required per-port incidence structure. Source-preserving gadget embedding remains an unproved obligation.
killed: A generic claim that orbit-rigidity by itself places the tau variables in an affine, majority, Horn/semilattice or otherwise universally tractable binary language.
A solver that discards source geometry and then appeals only to generic tractability of the rigid binary orbit relations.
The hope that the v7.2 rigid-gain compilation leaves a weak binary orbit language: it is already binary-relationally complete under pp composition.
positive: The hard expressive jump is now localized even more sharply: it is already present at the three-state orbit layer, before non-rigid gain sets are needed.
Any surviving polynomial route must exploit the Hamiltonian/Euler/port geometry or the correlated S3 holonomy structure, not merely the finite-domain relation type.
The explicit NEQ certificate gives a four-variable constant gadget target for a source-preserving embedding test.

next_target.name: E8_RIGID_NEQ_SOURCE_PRESERVING_EULER_PORT_EMBEDDING_OR_GEOMETRIC_OBSTRUCTION_V7_4
next_target.directive: Do not classify more abstract binary clones. Test whether the explicit A AND (B composed C) NEQ gadget can actually be embedded repeatedly inside the smooth-C4 Hamiltonian quotient while satisfying: one global supplied Euler tour, each C4 port incident with exactly two Hamiltonian half-edges, simple original graph, smooth inner cycles, and polynomial-size gadget composition. If yes, freeze a source-preserving NP-hard rigid sublanguage barrier. If no, identify and prove the exact Euler/port conservation law that prevents arbitrary pp wiring; that conservation law is the next possible algorithmic leverage. Mandatory controls include the v7.1 holonomy triangle and the Fleischner--Sabidussi source family.
